POLICY_TIERS.tier_0_no_conflict: single version or unanimous → omit conflictResolution field
POLICY_TIERS.tier_1_majority: >=2 workers agree on same contentHash → pick that hash; chosen workerId = lexicographically smallest among winners
POLICY_TIERS.tier_2_lexicographic_fallback: no unique winner with >=2 votes → pick lexicographically smallest workerId among ALL versions; rationale documents the fallback

PROVENANCE_PRESERVED: YES — conflictVersions lists all other versions on every record; conflictResolution appears on every record for the same path with isAuthoritative=true only on the chosen one
note: Written post-push to avoid the G7-18 chicken-and-egg metadata bug. The MAIN G7-19B commit (this HEAD) contains everything except final-head.json itself. The NEXT commit on top will add this file. The 'majority-then-lexicographic' policy is deterministic and transparent: it picks the majority version when >=2 workers agree, and falls back to lexicographic workerId when all disagree. The Tier 2 fallback is arbitrary (it may not pick the semantically correct version) — the rationale string documents this, and all conflicting versions remain in conflictVersions so downstream verification can override.
